result.title: When and How Does Muon Precondition? The Role of Structured Gradient Noise
result.summary: Muon has become a popular optimizer for large language model training, yet its theoretical foundations remain poorly understood. In this work, we study how gradient noise geometry shapes Muon's preconditioning benefits. We first show, theoretically and empirically, that under the classical isotropic noise assumption, Muon offers no acceleration beyond a rescaling of the learning rate. This motivates us to investigate structured noise arising from mini-batch sampling in associative memory with heterogeneous task frequencies. We establish an exact balancing threshold for two tasks and extend the analysis to multiple tasks, revealing how task coverage and gradient reliability jointly shape learning. Our analysis shows that Muon can soften the dependence on task frequency from linear to square-root, helping balance the learning of frequent and rare tasks. We further identify rotation-induced negative transfer in SignSGD that Muon avoids, and explain how momentum reduces sampling noise while tracking changing gradients. Controlled numerical experiments validate these mechanisms, and a preliminary LLM pretraining study illustrates the practical promise of fast-slow momentum.

AI.brief_summary: 该文从梯度噪声几何角度分析 Muon 预条件为何有效：证明在等向噪声假设下 Muon 仅等价于学习率缩放，进而在多任务频率不均的联想记忆设定下给出两任务精确平衡阈值并推广到多任务，说明 Muon 可把对任务频率的依赖从线性降为平方根，并讨论 SignSGD 的旋转负迁移与动量抑噪作用。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「结构化噪声 + fast-slow 动量」的训练机制可供核查是否适用于多任务 LVR 训练中稀有推理技能监督稀疏、频繁与罕见任务失衡导致的梯度可靠性差异，但与原论文视觉推理主线无直接联系，迁移性需人工核实。
